subject: Microbiology
title: Gram-Positive Cocci & Bacilli Identification Algorithm
preview: A small set of laboratory principles distinguishes major gram-positive cocci and bacilli before species-level confirmation.

sections.title: Catalase and arrangement
points: Clusters of gram-positive cocci suggest staphylococci; chains or pairs suggest streptococci or enterococci, with exceptions.
Catalase testing can support the initial separation, but technique and specimen quality matter.

sections.title: Coagulase and additional identification
points: Coagulase positivity is associated with Staphylococcus aureus; other staphylococci require appropriate species-level assessment.
Hemolysis patterns and targeted confirmatory tests support streptococcal and enterococcal differentiation.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Neither microscopic shape nor one bench test is sufficient for all clinical decisions.
Clinical relevance depends on the specimen source, contamination risk, patient status and susceptibility.

quickRevision: Gram-positive cocci are first grouped by arrangement and catalase results.
Staphylococci are typically catalase positive; streptococci and enterococci are typically catalase negative.
Culture features and biochemical tests are interpreted together, with species confirmation as needed.

quiz.question: Which test usually differentiates staphylococci from streptococci?
quiz.explanation: Gram-Positive Cocci Algorithm: • Catalase Test: Positive = Staphylococcus ; Negative = Streptococcus.
